title: Per-user throughput subsidy model
body:
Purpose / context:
- Quick personal scratchpad to test the idea of subsidizing per-user throughput for early-stage customers (reduce friction for product-led growth while protecting unit economics).
- Want a lightweight formula I can share with growth/solutions for initial offers.

Assumptions (plausible knobs to change):
- GPU cost (fully loaded, on-demand equivalent) = $4.0 / GPU-hour (can substitute reserved rate later).
- Serving efficiency: 50k tokens generated per GPU-hour baseline (conservative).
- Avg session: 1.2k tokens (prompt+response aggregated).
- Active sessions per MAU per month: 8
- MAU = 10,000 example customer
- Margin target: gross margin >= 60% (after infra cost) for hosted payg offers

Base definitions / conversions:
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = 50_000
- tokens_per_session = 1_200
- sessions_per_user_month = 8
- tokens_per_user_month = tokens_per_session * sessions_per_user_month = 9_600
- gpu_hours_per_user_month = tokens_per_user_month / tokens_per_gpu_hour = 9_600 / 50_000 = 0.192 hours (~11.5 minutes)
- infra_cost_per_user_month = gpu_hours_per_user_month * $4.0 = $0.768

Interpretation:
- At these baseline numbers, raw GPU infra is <$1/user/month. This is surprising but consistent with small per-user active consumption. If users are more conversational (long sessions / continuous chat), tokens bump up fast.

Edge scenario: heavy convo app (agent-like)
- tokens_per_session = 6k, sessions_per_user = 20
- tokens_per_user_month = 120k -> gpu_hours = 120k/50k = 2.4h -> infra_cost = 2.4 * $4 = $9.6/user/month.
- Huge difference. So tiering by "interaction shape" matters more than raw MAU.

Design idea: throughput subsidy + shape buckets
- Offer a "starter throughput subsidy" for new accounts: cover first N tokens per MAU per month (e.g., first 10k tokens / user-month) at 0 cost to customer for 3 months. Aligns with above baseline (9.6k).
- Introduce 3 shape buckets (per-customer):
  * Lightweight: expected tokens/user/month <= 20k (low cost).
  * Conversational: 20k - 200k
  * Agent/Heavy: >200k (requires Dedicated or reserved pricing)
- Routing: for customers in Lightweight, keep hosted PAYG with subsidy. For Conversational, suggest hybrid (Dedicated light) or higher per-token price. For Heavy, require Dedicated commit.

Subsidy math examples (starter credit model):
- Starter: first 10k tokens/user-month free for 3 months. For 10k tokens -> gpu_hours = 0.2 -> cost = $0.8 (per user-month). For 10k * 1k users = cost $800/mo covered.
- Tradeoffs: good for activation, but attackers/bots can game. Need rate-limits + bot detection + per-account caps.

Per-route / UI tier idea (convex pricing):
- Small bucket: 0-25k tokens/user-month -> $2 / user-month (covers infra + margin)
- Mid bucket: 25k-150k -> $0.0007 / token (or equivalently $17.5 for 25k tokens baseline)
- Heavy: >150k -> recommend commit / dedicated: e.g., $0.0005 / token with commit discounts and throughput SLOs

Back-of-the-envelope margin check: (use mid bucket)
- Suppose user consumes 50k tokens/month -> infra cost = 50k/50k * $4 = $4 -> If we charge $12 for that bucket (or $0.00024/token), gross margin = (12-4)/12 = 66% -> meets target.
- But if serving efficiency changes (quantization/opt improvements) and tokens_per_gpu_hour becomes 100k, infra halves and margin improves. So include dynamic suggestions in console/optimize product.

Credit / burst mechanism (protecting RU):
- Keep free starter tokens but meter bursts: e.g., free tokens only applicable if avg token/sec per session < threshold. That prevents heavy one-user attacks.
- Implement decaying credits: free credits are consumed preferentially, then a per-minute token budget enforced.

Operational controls to avoid abuse:
- Require card up front + minimal verification for starter subsidy.
- Soft SLO: if detected average tokens/user_month > 3x expected bucket, create nudges + limit until manual review.

Notes on selling to mid-market: incentives to commit -> discounted per-token + predictable throughput (Dedicated). Example: commit 10M tokens/month -> blended cost negotiated vs per-token.

Quick sensitivity table (manual):
- tokens_per_gpu_hour: 30k / 50k / 100k
- cost_per_gpu_hour: $3 / $4 / $6
- compute infra per user @ 10k tokens:
  * (30k, $3): gpu_hours = 0.333 -> cost = $1.00
  * (50k, $4): gpu_hours = 0.2 -> cost = $0.8
  * (100k, $6): gpu_hours = 0.1 -> cost = $0.6

Open questions / risks:
- How to detect "shape" automatically? Heuristics: median session length, avg tokens/session, sessions/day. Need instrumentation hooks in console and trial onboarding script.
- Abuse vectors: free credits exploited by automated scripts. Need quota per-email/phone and startup verification.
- Upsell path: how to surface to growth teams when a customer is trending to "conversational" so they can pitch Dedicated.
- Billing complexity: multiple knobs (per-user price + per-token overage + credits) could confuse sales. Keep UX simple: highlight "what's included" per plan.

Next steps (short):
- Build a toy calculator sheet (inputs: tokens_per_gpu_hour, gpu_cost, tokens_per_session, sessions_per_user) so PMs/SEs can play. (I will create and share)
- Draft copy for growth onboarding: "Starter: first 10k tokens/user-month free for 3 months" with clear limits.
- Discuss detection heuristics with product-analytics + infra to ensure metrics available.

Random scratch thoughts:
- Consider token-weighted daily active user (twDAU) metric for funnel instead of MAU to weight for heavy users.
- Could offer "session bundles" (e.g., 100 sessions included per user-month) for UX-forward pricing instead of token counts. Easier for non-technical buyers.

End of notes.

(rough, messy — will tidy if we take forward)
